documents.text: Alexandria reminders have no background timer. A pending reminder becomes deliverable when its due time passes, but it is consumed only when a client next calls check_reminders. Without a client there is no delivery; the server reaches nobody by itself.

Reminder delivery is query-time consumption by check_reminders, not a scheduled push. Clients call this tool to consume due occurrences. A conditional claim provides best-effort-once delivery; recurring rows advance past now and coalesce missed occurrences.

heat_state.last_accessed_at is the spacing reference and moves only on an actual record_access. The separate last_touched field anchors the stored heat value. Decay materialization must never change last_accessed_at.

A heat sweep updates decayed heat and last_touched, but leaves last_accessed_at untouched. Otherwise an hourly sweep becomes the spacing reference even when nobody retrieves the memory. Real accesses alone update the access clock.

The native Rust Burn Granite provider emits 768-dimensional FP32 vectors using CLS pooling and L2 normalization with FP64 accumulation cast back to FP32. CPU is default; explicit ROCm or Vulkan needs its compiled backend and available device. There is no CPU fallback for a failed GPU request.

Granite owns one serial native Rust inference worker, with one active job and one queued job. CPU and GPU share the same 768D FP32 CLS-pooled, L2-normalized embedding space. Inputs have exact sequence lengths; microbatch size is one. Cancelling active work discards delivery rather than interrupting a kernel.

A fresh separate-target offline migration never opens the original source storage engine. On Linux it opens the existing root LOCK read-only, takes an exclusive nonblocking lock, and holds it through copying. Missing or live locks fail without creating or writing the lock file.

Offline migration reads source identity only from the copied target, never by opening the source engine. The source is protected by its existing read-only LOCK during the original copy. Resume validates the adjacent original source receipt, journal and original non-vector baseline; it does not recapture partially rewritten data.
